sentences.text: The only known species in the genus is Rhomaleopakhus turpanensis. The genus name combines Greek words meaning "robust" and "forearm", while the species name refers to the Turpan Basin where the specimen was collected.
As a mamenchisaurid sauropod, it was likely a large, four-legged herbivore. The animal is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.

The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in 1993 by a Chinese-Japanese expedition near Qiketai in Shanshan, Xinjiang province. The genus was named by Upchurch and colleagues in 2021.

Researchers noted that the robust forelimb evolved convergently in core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa, titanosaurs, and ceratopsids. Researchers believe the robust forelimb correlates with a flexed forearm orientation, an enhanced role in feeding, and a forward shift in the center of mass.
It is possible that these animals specialized in a feeding strategy involving efficient movement between scattered food sources.

Fossils are known from the lower section of the Kalaza Formation in China's Turpan and Junggar Basins. The Kalaza Formation dates to the Late Jurassic, lying above Middle Jurassic rocks and below Early Cretaceous layers. The formation consists of thick red sandstones and mudstones deposited in terrestrial or river environments.

During the Late Jurassic, the environment was warm and seasonally dry with alluvial deltas, transitioning to arid conditions toward the Cretaceous. The dinosaur lived in the Late Jurassic Kalaza Formation of China. It lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 145 million years ago in the Tithonian stage, in what is now Asia. The time range for the genus is the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 143.1 million years ago.
